mapper.content:
Hi {{10.`First Name`}},

A surprising number of Oxford planning applications are delayed before they are even assessed, often because of relatively small validation issues.

We recently hosted a CPD session for architects looking at why this happens and how delays can often be avoided across heritage, ecology and constrained Oxford sites.

I’d sent over an invitation previously, but thought the recording may still be useful to you given the type of work your practice is involved in.

The session was titled:
Inside Oxford Planning: Why Applications Stall and How To Get Them Moving.

Andrew Murdoch, Development Management Service Manager at Oxford City Council, shared the council-side perspective on where delays commonly arise, while the wider discussion explored how ecology, BNG, heritage, flood risk and design review increasingly need to be considered much earlier in the process.

You can watch the recording here:
https://www.carmaukconstruction.co.uk/aprilcpd

Hopefully there’s something in it that proves useful on a future project.

We’re currently planning the next CPD for September, and I’d be very happy to send over details once confirmed if that would be of interest?

Hope your team’s been busy with some interesting work recently.

Best regards,

Paul Sellers
CEO
M: 07719 338653

Hi {{10.`First Name`}},

I reached out previously to invite you to a CPD session we hosted for architects working in and around Oxford. If you missed the earlier email, or weren’t able to attend, I thought the recording may still be useful to you.

The session was titled:
Inside Oxford Planning: Why Applications Stall and How To Get Them Moving.

One of the more interesting points discussed was that a significant number of applications are delayed before they are even assessed because of relatively simple validation issues — things like plan discrepancies, missing tree or TPO information, incorrect forms, fee errors or incomplete supporting information.

Andrew Murdoch, Development Management Service Manager at Oxford City Council, shared the council-side perspective on where these delays commonly arise and how they can often be avoided.

The session also explored how ecology, BNG, heritage, flood risk and design review increasingly need to be considered much earlier in the process on Oxford schemes, particularly on constrained or sensitive sites.

You can watch the recording here:
https://www.carmaukconstruction.co.uk/aprilcpd

Hopefully there’s something in it that proves useful on a future project.

We’re currently planning the next CPD for September, and I’d be very happy to send over details once confirmed if that would be of interest?

Have a good day.

Best regards,

Paul Sellers
CEO
M: 07719 338653
